identity.name: EMAIL — Thread-Hijack Reply-Chain Phishing (Proofpoint TAP + Microsoft 365)
identity.summary: The email_emitter emits a Proofpoint TAP messagesDelivered event for a reply-chain hijack re-using an existing subject from a compromised partner mailbox plus a clicksPermitted event for one recipient, then proves the same hijack logic fires over the Microsoft 365 EmailEvents shape. Cortex XSIAM raises a thread-hijack phishing alert and stitches the permitted click to the endpoint follow-on.
identity.description: Thread-hijack (reply-chain) phishing inserts a malicious reply into a legitimate, already-trusted conversation, typically from a compromised partner or internal mailbox (T1566.002 carried inside an existing thread, often pivoting to internal spearphishing T1534). Because the message re-uses a real subject and trusted sender it bypasses the recipient's skepticism. This card drives CortexSim's email_emitter to POST a Proofpoint TAP messagesDelivered event (in_reply_to_existing_subject marker, classification=phish) and a clicksPermitted event for ada.lovelace into the email log collector, then repeats the pattern in Microsoft 365 / Defender for Office 365 EmailEvents shape. Detection is email-log analytics in Cortex XSIAM: an XQL rule over the proofpoint_tap_raw dataset flags phish-classified messages delivered into an existing reply chain, with a follow-on query proving the permitted click. A correlation rule fuses the delivered-then-clicked hijack with the recipient's endpoint follow-on into one incident.

prerequisites.description: CortexSim email_emitter EAL plugin registered and an authorized email log collector endpoint reachable.
prerequisites.check_command: python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli describe email_emitter | jq -e '.eal_targets | length > 0'

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM ingesting the Proofpoint TAP (proofpoint_tap_raw) and Microsoft 365 (msft_o365) email datasets.

payload.code:
# Emit a thread-hijack reply-chain phishing message (Proofpoint TAP then Microsoft 365 shape).
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/email-004.yml --live
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/email-004-m365.yml --live

expected_artifacts.description: A delivered reply-chain message re-using an existing subject plus a permitted click for one recipient classified as phish.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: classification = "phish" and in_reply_to_existing_subject = true for one recipient

expected_artifacts.description: Outbound HTTPS POST burst from the scenario runner to the email log collector.

iocs.context: Compromised partner sender domain carrying the reply-chain hijack (email_emitter thread_hijack indicators). Appears in the Proofpoint TAP senderDomain / M365 SenderMailFromDomain field.
Malicious URL inserted into the trusted reply chain (email_emitter thread_hijack indicators). Appears in threatsInfoMap.threatUrl / M365 Url and is the clicked link.
Compromised partner sender address re-using an existing subject (email_emitter thread_hijack indicators). Pivot for the thread-hijack incident.

biocs.name: EMAIL-004 Pre-Flight email_emitter Metadata Visible
biocs.description: Pre-flight: email_emitter metadata visible to operator. Confirms the EAL plugin is registered and exposes EMAIL targets before any events are emitted, so a null result means a harness fault rather than a detection miss.
biocs.logic:
dataset = proofpoint_tap_raw
| filter messageType in ("messagesBlocked", "messagesDelivered", "clicksPermitted") or _raw_log contains "email_emitter"
| comp count() as preflight_events by recipient
| filter preflight_events >= 0

xql_queries.name: EMAIL-004 Thread-Hijack Reply-Chain Phishing Delivered
xql_queries.query:
// [MODEL: dataset=proofpoint_tap_raw, content_id="ProofpointTAP"]
dataset = proofpoint_tap_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter classification = "phish" and messageType = "messagesDelivered" and in_reply_to_existing_subject = true
| comp count() as hijack_events, values(sender) as senders, values(threatUrl) as urls by recipient
| filter hijack_events >= 1
| fields recipient, senders, urls, hijack_events

xql_queries.name: EMAIL-004 Thread-Hijack Permitted Click Follow-On
xql_queries.query:
dataset = proofpoint_tap_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter messageType = "clicksPermitted" and classification = "phish"
| comp count() as click_events, values(threatUrl) as clicked_urls by recipient, sender
| filter click_events >= 1
| fields recipient, sender, click_events, clicked_urls

correlation_rules.name: Thread-Hijack Reply-Chain Phishing — Email to Endpoint Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(EMAIL-004 Thread-Hijack Reply-Chain Phishing Delivered) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(EMAIL-004 Thread-Hijack Permitted Click Follow-On) THEN xdr_data endpoint process for the same recipient within 1h

analytics_modules: Cortex XSIAM Email Analytics — Reply-chain hijack phish delivered into existing subject
Cortex XSIAM Correlation — Hijack delivered-then-clicked to endpoint stitch

products.evidence_query: dataset = proofpoint_tap_raw | filter classification = "phish" and in_reply_to_existing_subject = true | comp count() by recipient | filter _count >= 1
Correlation CR-EMAIL-0004 fuses the delivered-then-clicked hijack with the recipient endpoint follow-on into one incident.

threat_scenarios.name: Thread-Hijack Reply-Chain Phishing Detection
threat_scenarios.description: Detect a malicious reply inserted into a trusted conversation across both Proofpoint TAP and Microsoft 365 email log shapes, stitched delivered-then-clicked to the endpoint follow-on.

threat_steps.objective: A phish-classified reply-chain message re-using an existing subject raises a thread-hijack alert.
preconditions: Cortex XSIAM ingesting proofpoint_tap_raw and msft_o365 datasets.
email_emitter authorized against the lab collector.
steps: Observe the thread-hijack phishing alert per recipient in the Cortex console.
success_criteria: XQL `EMAIL-004 Thread-Hijack Reply-Chain Phishing Delivered` returns >= 1 row.
XQL `EMAIL-004 Thread-Hijack Permitted Click Follow-On` returns >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: The delivered-then-clicked hijack stitches to the endpoint follow-on.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-EMAIL-0004` groups the hijack delivery, the permitted click, and the recipient endpoint follow-on under one incident.

preventive_controls: Re-evaluate trust on replies whose sender authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) degrades mid-thread.
Rewrite and detonate URLs even inside existing reply chains.
Alert recipients when a long-trusted partner sender's infrastructure changes abruptly.
detection_engineering: Flag phish-classified messages delivered into an existing subject/reply chain.
Correlate the delivered hijack with the subsequent permitted click for the same recipient.
Stitch the email hijack to the recipient endpoint/identity follow-on.
